items.answer: They can be scaled to any size without losing quality; file sizes are usually smaller for simple images; individual objects can be edited separately.

items.stem: Explain why photographs are stored as bitmaps rather than vectors.

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'bitmap (raster) graphic' and 'vector graphic'.
items.answer: bitmap (raster) graphic: An image stored as a grid of pixels, each with a colour value. vector graphic: An image stored as a list of objects (lines, shapes, curves) described by mathematical properties such as coordinates, colour and line width.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: bitmap (raster) graphic correctly described; 1 mark: vector graphic correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'pixelation' and 'vector graphic'.
items.answer: pixelation: The blocky appearance of a bitmap image when it is enlarged so much that individual pixels become visible. vector graphic: An image stored as a list of objects (lines, shapes, curves) described by mathematical properties such as coordinates, colour and line width.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: pixelation correctly described; 1 mark: vector graphic correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Which file format is most suitable for a screenshot with sharp text and a transparent background?
items.answer: PNG
items.markingKey: PNG: bitmap, lossless compression; supports transparency.

items.stem: Lina is designing a logo, posters and website images for Peak Fitness in Colombo. (a) Explain why the logo should be created as a vector graphic. (b) Describe the difference between lossy and lossless compression.
items.answer: (a) Scales to any size (business card to billboard) without losing quality; editable objects; small file. (b) Lossy permanently removes data for smaller files; lossless reduces size with no data lost.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark each. [2]

items.stem: Lakeside College in Seoul needs a new logo and product photographs for its website. (a) Explain why the logo should be created as a vector graphic. (b) Recommend a file format for the product photographs and justify your choice.
items.answer: (a) Scales to any size (business card to billboard) without losing quality; editable objects; small file. (b) JPEG — small files via lossy compression, good for photos.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark format; 1 mark justification. [2]

items.stem: State what is meant by 'z-order'.
items.answer: The stacking order of objects, which decides which object appears in front when objects overlap.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: The stacking order of objects, which decides which object appears in front when objects overlap. [2]

items.stem: Distinguish between 'layer' and 'gradient fill'.
items.answer: layer: A separate level in a graphic on which objects are placed; objects on higher layers appear in front of those on lower layers. gradient fill: A fill that changes smoothly from one colour to another across an object (linear or radial).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: layer correctly described; 1 mark: gradient fill correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'grouping' and 'node (anchor point)'.
items.answer: grouping: Combining several objects so that they can be moved, resized or formatted together as a single object. node (anchor point): A point on a vector path that can be moved to change the shape of the path.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: grouping correctly described; 1 mark: node (anchor point) correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: A vector graphic has these overlapping objects, listed from front (top) to back: Title text, Logo, Banner, Background. The designer then applies, in order: Send Backward on Logo; Bring to Front on Banner. (Bring Forward / Send Backward move an object one place.) State the new order from front to back.
items.answer: Banner, Title text, Logo, Background
items.markingKey: Final order front to back: Banner, Title text, Logo, Background (lose 1 mark per object out of place). [2]

items.stem: A vector logo group is 80 mm wide and 20 mm high. With the aspect ratio locked, its width is changed to 60 mm. Calculate the new height and the percentage scale factor.
Lucas is creating a vector poster for an event run by Harbour Bank in Singapore. Explain why the aspect ratio should be maintained when resizing the logo.
items.answer: Prevents distortion so the brand looks correct.
items.markingKey: 1 mark distortion; 1 mark brand image. [2]

items.stem: A designer at Nova Telecom in Santiago is editing the company's vector logo. (a) Describe how a gradient fill could be used. (b) Explain why the aspect ratio should be maintained when resizing the logo.
items.answer: (a) A smooth blend of colours, e.g. sky from dark to light blue, linear or radial. (b) Prevents distortion so the brand looks correct.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark description; 1 mark example. [2] (b) 1 mark distortion; 1 mark brand image. [2]

items.stem: A designer at Nova Telecom in Accra is editing the company's vector logo. Discuss the use of vector graphics software rather than bitmap software for the designs of Nova Telecom.
items.answer: Points for: scalable artwork; editable objects, layers and groups; small files. Points against / limitations: not suitable for photo editing; learning curve; some effects are easier in bitmap software. Conclusion: vector software suits logos and posters; bitmap software suits photographs — designers often use both.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: scalable artwork; editable objects, layers and groups; small files. Against: not suitable for photo editing; learning curve; some effects are easier in bitmap software. Conclusion may argue: vector software suits logos and posters; bitmap software suits photographs — designers often use both. [4]

items.stem: Define the term 'filter'.
items.answer: An effect applied to a bitmap that changes pixel values, such as blur, sharpen or sepia.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: An effect applied to a bitmap that changes pixel values, such as blur, sharpen or sepia. [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): Enlarging a bitmap can cause pixelation. Reason (R): Fewer pixels are stored. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'cropping' and 'mask'.
items.answer: cropping: Removing unwanted outer parts of an image to improve its composition or change its shape. mask: A layer that hides or reveals parts of an image without permanently deleting pixels, so edits can be applied to selected areas.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cropping correctly described; 1 mark: mask correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Riverside Medical Centre in Nairobi is producing a printed brochure from photographs taken by its staff. Explain why the photographs should be cropped.
items.answer: Remove distracting background; focus on subject; fit layout shape.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Meridian Hospital in Dubai is producing a printed brochure from photographs taken by its staff. (a) Explain why the images should be resized before use on the website. (b) Describe how a mask could be used.
items.answer: (a) Smaller dimensions and files load faster; match the space on the page. (b) Hide the background or apply an effect to only part of the image without deleting pixels.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each. [2] (b) 1 mark hide/select; 1 mark non-destructive. [2]

items.stem: Omar is preparing photographs of staff and products for the website of Sunrise Bakery in Dhaka. (a) Explain why the images should be resized before use on the website. (b) Describe how a mask could be used. (c) Describe two filters that could be applied.
items.answer: (a) Smaller dimensions and files load faster; match the space on the page. (b) Hide the background or apply an effect to only part of the image without deleting pixels. (c) Sharpen; blur; sepia/greyscale; noise reduction; vignette.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each. [2] (b) 1 mark hide/select; 1 mark non-destructive. [2] (c) 1 mark each, max 2. [2]
